transition.interpretation: Both maker-positive B2 candidates observed in the previous live window cease to be maker-positive in the next observed live window on the same main revision. One transition is not a statistical rejection of B2 alpha, but a one-window positive static frontier is not persistence evidence.

binary_hurdle_interpretation.reason: The live V5 multi-leg broker does not force-buy missing legs as taker when maker completion is insufficient. The maker-vs-taker binary mixture cannot be used as the live broker's expected-PnL model.

runtime_broker_semantics.timeout_action: cancel remaining passive orders then unwind only filled inventory at executable bids with protocol fee and configured slippage

research_conclusion.material_change: The two maker-positive B2 rows from the previous live window disappear in the next observed live window on the same main revision; the next frontier has 39 raw-positive B2 rows but zero maker-positive rows.
research_conclusion.reason: Static maker positivity is currently transient rather than recurrent, while no direct event-time B2 sample estimates the live broker's partial-completion, excess-fill, cancel-latency, timeout-unwind and markout economics.
research_conclusion.next_measurement: Collect prospective B2 maker-positive frontier snapshots and prioritize event-time replay only after recurrence is observed. For recurrent candidates, use strictly pre-arrival microprice, spread, L1/L3/L5 depth and imbalance, OFI, queue state and measured latency; record per-leg fill hazards, common completion, excess inventory, cancel-latency fills, timeout unwind PnL, and 45s/60s/300s markout under 1x/1.5x/2x queue/latency/slippage stress.
research_conclusion.acceptance_target: Positive common-sample expected net execution PnL under the actual partial-completion/unwind contract plus prospective recurrence. A one-window positive maker edge is insufficient.
